{"artifact":"SmeDossierEnvelope","schema_version":"0.4.0","stage_id":"02.dossier_sections","probe":"rdmv-fl-e","lineage":{"input_manifest_sha256":"bd4386ffb7a655bbf778eff2da67374ef6770bfbd3899c00f0002c0ee0632474","candidate_lineage_id":"2026-10-28-rdmv-fl-class-e:lineage:37","source_registry_sha256":"b17b1a3691c9724cc739459037987900e5b1edce40443ad13e42b6eee3e12974","source_liveness_sha256":"0968940df7e2ea0794d4b4ea984515bb41aeba17bada73f538009ca9e9f9cf7a"},"envelope_scope":{"kind":"partial_chunk","assigned_section_ids":["C"],"chunk_index":1,"chunk_total":1},"section_char_limit":12000,"sections":[{"section_id":"C","chunk_id":"C.01","merge_seq":1,"domain":"Handling Emergencies","heading":"C - Handling Emergencies","learner_facing":true,"markdown":"## C - Handling Emergencies

FACT_ID: sec09-F01 | anchor: A01
Defensive driving adapts to weather, self, and others, scans for danger, predicts moves, and guards intersections hardest [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-fl-e:florida-department-of-highway-safety-and:handbook:pdf-0083]

FACT_ID: sec09-F02 | anchor: A01
Forced crashes prefer roadside over oncoming lanes, driven exits over skids, still targets over moving ones, same-way taps over head-ons, and hedges over trees [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-fl-e:florida-department-of-highway-safety-and:handbook:pdf-0083]

FACT_ID: sec09-F03 | anchor: A01
Stops start with signaled pullovers, killed engines and audio, seated riders, and visible hands [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-fl-e:florida-department-of-highway-safety-and:handbook:pdf-0083]

FACT_ID: sec09-F04 | anchor: A02
Stops continue with lit cabins or lowered tint, followed orders, either-side officers, opened windows, declared weapons, and unreached documents [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-fl-e:florida-department-of-highway-safety-and:handbook:pdf-0084]

FACT_ID: sec09-F05 | anchor: A02
Officers show plainclothes credentials, explain stops, and collect licenses, insurance, and registrations with announced reaches [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-fl-e:florida-department-of-highway-safety-and:handbook:pdf-0084]

FACT_ID: sec09-F06 | anchor: A02
Stops close with visible-handed exits, warnings, tickets, or arrests, clarified questions, court contests, signed-but-innocent tickets, and supervisor requests [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-fl-e:florida-department-of-highway-safety-and:handbook:pdf-0084]

FACT_ID: sec09-F07 | anchor: A03
Crash duty stops, calls 911 or star-FHP, flashes hazards, aids the hurt, clears minor blockers, swaps full details, and sketches scenes [A03].
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-fl-e:florida-department-of-highway-safety-and:handbook:pdf-0085]

FACT_ID: sec09-F08 | anchor: A03
Officers write DUI, death, injury, and tow crashes, while drivers self-report the rest to the state within 10 days [A03].
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-fl-e:florida-department-of-highway-safety-and:handbook:pdf-0085]

FACT_ID: sec09-F09 | anchor: A03
Unattended strikes hunt owners with officer notice, else leave name, contact, and plate notes [A03].
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-fl-e:florida-department-of-highway-safety-and:handbook:pdf-0085]

FACT_ID: sec09-F10 | anchor: A03
Fleeing death brings first-degree felony time of four years minimum, serious hurt second-degree, plain injury third-degree, all with three-year license loss, and attended-property hits bring misdemeanors [A03].
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-fl-e:florida-department-of-highway-safety-and:handbook:pdf-0085]

FACT_ID: sec09-F11 | anchor: A03
First-aid arrivals call anyway, park far and lit, exit clear of traffic, freeze spine cases, and leave helmets on [A03].
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-fl-e:florida-department-of-highway-safety-and:handbook:pdf-0085]

FACT_ID: sec09-F12 | anchor: A04
Shock care calms victims, withholds drinks, lays them flat with raised legs, blankets warmth, and opens airways [A04].
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-fl-e:florida-department-of-highway-safety-and:handbook:pdf-0086]

FACT_ID: sec09-F13 | anchor: A04
Rear-end defense holds four seconds, checks brake lamps, mirrors around, signals early, eases stops, and flows with traffic [A04].
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-fl-e:florida-department-of-highway-safety-and:handbook:pdf-0086]

FACT_ID: sec09-F14 | anchor: A04
Breakdowns clear all four wheels, show 200 feet both ways, flash hazards, unload roadside passengers, and call for help [A04].
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-fl-e:florida-department-of-highway-safety-and:handbook:pdf-0086]

FACT_ID: sec09-F15 | anchor: A04
Traction-loss stops pump plain brakes but stomp, hold, and steer anti-locks, easing only locking front wheels [A04].
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-fl-e:florida-department-of-highway-safety-and:handbook:pdf-0086]

FACT_ID: sec09-F16 | anchor: A05
Car fires exit first, call 911, fight small blazes with extinguishers only, never water fuel, and flee fumes and blasts [A05].
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-fl-e:florida-department-of-highway-safety-and:handbook:pdf-0087]

FACT_ID: sec09-F17 | anchor: A05
Jammed pedals lift feet, clutch or neutralize, press brakes without slamming, and steer safe, killing engines only as a steering-costly last resort [A05].
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-fl-e:florida-department-of-highway-safety-and:handbook:pdf-0087]

FACT_ID: sec09-F18 | anchor: A05
Overcorrection rolls cars through sharp panic steering, so road exits stay calm, firm, gas-free, unslammed, and gently guided [A05].
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-fl-e:florida-department-of-highway-safety-and:handbook:pdf-0087]

FACT_ID: sec09-F19 | anchor: A05
Dead-signal crossings run four-way with arrival order and left-yields-right ties [A05].
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-fl-e:florida-department-of-highway-safety-and:handbook:pdf-0087]

FACT_ID: sec09-F20 | anchor: A05
Pavement drops coast straight with firm wheels and light brakes, rejoining slowly with signals when clear [A05].
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-fl-e:florida-department-of-highway-safety-and:handbook:pdf-0087]

FACT_ID: sec09-F21 | anchor: A05
Skids lift gas, spare brakes, and steer into the slide toward the goal [A05].
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-fl-e:florida-department-of-highway-safety-and:handbook:pdf-0087]

FACT_ID: sec09-F22 | anchor: A05
Track stalls empty everyone instantly away, since trains need at least 20 seconds past flashing [A05].
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-fl-e:florida-department-of-highway-safety-and:handbook:pdf-0087]

FACT_ID: sec09-F23 | anchor: A06
Train comers run 45 degrees toward steel to dodge debris, then call out, and blue crossing signs list railroad rescue numbers [A06].
Source: [A06 -> src:rdmv-fl-e:florida-department-of-highway-safety-and:handbook:pdf-0088]

FACT_ID: sec09-F24 | anchor: A06
Sinking cars float 30 to 60 seconds, so riders unbuckle, window out before doors flood, kick side glass, and keep escape tools handy [A06].
Source: [A06 -> src:rdmv-fl-e:florida-department-of-highway-safety-and:handbook:pdf-0088]

FACT_ID: sec09-F25 | anchor: A06
Blowouts coast brake-free with steered slowdowns, soft pedals when settled, and full roadside exits [A06].
Source: [A06 -> src:rdmv-fl-e:florida-department-of-highway-safety-and:handbook:pdf-0088]

FACT_ID: sec09-F26 | anchor: A06
Wrong-way comers earn horns, flashes, hard brakes, and roadside steers [A06].
Source: [A06 -> src:rdmv-fl-e:florida-department-of-highway-safety-and:handbook:pdf-0088]

FACT_ID: sec09-F27 | anchor: A06
Wet brakes test lightly, pull or fade, and dry under slow low-gear pedaling [A06].
Source: [A06 -> src:rdmv-fl-e:florida-department-of-highway-safety-and:handbook:pdf-0088]
